abstract: Small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a neuroendocrine carcinoma characterized by early metastasis, rapid emergence of therapy resistance, and dismal patient outcomes. SCLC subtypes have been proposed based on expression of lineage transcription factors ASCL1, NEUROD1, and POU2F3 and the level of inflammation. To further discern biologically distinct subsets, we apply non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) to gene expression data from 146 SCLC patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. We identify three ASCL1-dominant and three NEUROD1-dominant subsets, an ASCL1/NEUROD1 co-active subset, and a REST-active low-neuroendocrine subset. These subsets differ in MYC family expression, transcription factor activation, antigen presentation transcriptional programs, and expression of cell surface molecules that represent therapeutic targets. Using a random forest classifier, we project these clusters onto 7 genetic mouse models of SCLC, human cell lines, and patient data from the IMpower133 clinical trial, allowing us to link PDX-derived subsets to specific murine and cellular models and to patient responses.
